summary: Microelectromechanical—so-called “MEMs”—vapor cells are a key component in atom-based quantum sensors, such as clocks, gyroscopes, electric field sensors, and magnetometers. title: Size and Shape of Condensing Steam Jets and Plumes
summary: Droplet-laden cloud dynamics emerge from coupled phase transitions and turbulent mixing. title: First Experimental Evidence of Helicon Current Drive
summary: Helicon current drive has been observed experimentally for the first time in dedicated DIII-D tokamak experiments, providing a proof-of-principle and an attractive source of efficient current drive in reactor-grade tokamak plasmas.

summary: Nanoscale hotspot thermal transport is critical for thermal management of electronic devices. Here, the thermal transport in nanoscale multiple hotspots is investigated by solving the phonon Boltzmann transport equation. summary: Graphene, through the coexistence of large cyclotron gaps and small spin and valley gaps, offers the possibility to study the breakdown of the quantum Hall effect (QHE) across a wide range of energy scales. title: Optical Readout of the Magnetic State Using Terahertz Electric Fields
summary: Resonant excitation of -electrons by a terahertz optical signal rotates the magnetization in rare-earth iron garnets, establishing a new ultrafast magnetoelectric coupling that can potentially be used for ultrafast magneto-optical readout in magnetic data storage.

summary: We extend the classical test particle insertion (TPI) method to anisotropic systems and develop an anisotropic test particle insertion (ATPI) framework that efficiently extracts anisotropic interaction potentials from dense fluids using a small number of equilibrium snapshots. The method leverages t…

title: Fast Solidification of a Gravity-Stretched Liquid Jet
summary: A new technique for generating solid fibers from a liquid jet is easier to model—and thus easier to control—than past methods.

summary: Microwave-induced resistance oscillations (MIROs) occur when a two-dimensional electron gas is subjected to radiation of frequency $ω=2πf$ and varying magnetic field $B$. title: Flavor-Polarized Chern Insulator in the Half-Filled Rhombohedral Graphene Moiré Superlattice
summary: At an even filling, a rhombohedral octalayer graphene moiré superlattice with electric-field-tunable chirality hosts a robust Chern insulating state.

title: Fluidic Hysterons and Memory in Flow Networks
summary: Soft elastic fibers in microfluidic channels can create a fluid system with memory of previous actions through a flow-structure feedback.

title: Breakdown of the Kerr-Cat Qubit Tunneling Time Induced by Auxiliary Circuit Modes
summary: Researchers show that auxiliary circuit modes trigger multiphoton resonances that break down Kerr-cat qubit coherence under strong driving.

title: Topological Mixed States: Phases of Matter from Axiomatic Approaches
summary: A quantum information framework classifies mixed-state topological phases for open quantum systems, introducing phase invariants based on an information convex set, memory capacity, and secret sharing.

title: Nature Is Stingy: Universality of Scrooge Ensembles in Quantum Many-Body Systems
summary: Researchers introduce Scrooge -designs to quantify how constrained quantum systems achieve universal randomness and deep thermalization.

title: Variational Multi-Gaussian Phase-Space Bosonic Dynamics via Automatic Differentiation
summary: Researchers introduce a variational multi-Gaussian phase-space method combining analytical techniques with automatic differentiation to reveal the critical dynamics of large open quantum bosonic lattices.

title: Chaotic Many-Body Quantum Dynamics, Spectral Correlations, and Energy Diffusion
summary: Researchers analyze a solvable many-body model to demonstrate how energy diffusion governs spectral correlations in chaotic quantum systems.

title: Exact Nematic and Mixed Magnetic Phases Driven by Competing Orders on the Pyrochlore Lattice
summary: Analysis of a frustrated pyrochlore spin model demonstrates that thermal fluctuations and parameter-dependent symmetries suppress conventional order to stabilize a magnetic nematic phase.

title: Pomeranchuk Instability Induced by an Emergent Higher-Order Van Hove Singularity on the Distorted Kagome Surface of ${\mathrm{Co}}_{3}{\mathrm{Sn}}_{2}{\mathrm{S}}_{2}$
summary: Surface deformation of the kagome lattice in flattens saddle points into a higher-order Van Hove singularity, triggering a -wave Pomeranchuk instability and nematic states.

title: Topological Flowscape Reveals State Transitions in Nonreciprocal Living Matter
summary: Characterizing living systems far from the thermodynamic limit can yield insight into the physics of nonreciprocity and biological self-organization.

title: Statistical Physics of Deep Learning: Optimal Learning of a Multilayer Perceptron near Interpolation
summary: Using statistical physics and random matrix theory, researchers derive the generalization error of a deep fully connected neural network and uncover the mechanisms governing its behavior as feature learning progressively propagates across layers.

title: Identifying Geometric Third-Order Nonlinear Transport in Disordered Materials
summary: A theoretical data-analysis tool resolves the chaotic interpretation of nonlinear electronic transport data, providing a structured method to extract quantum geometric properties from realistic materials.

title: Waves Maintain Large-Scale 2D Flows in Rotating Turbulence and Cause Their Demise
summary: A first-principles approach helps explain energy transfer from 3D wave excitation to 2D structures in rotating turbulent flow.

title: Topological Defect Propagation to Classify Knitted Fabrics
summary: The ability of a fabric to be knitted into a textile can be determined on the basis of the topology of its pattern.

title: Autonomous Stabilization of Remote Entanglement in a Cascaded Quantum Network
summary: Researchers have achieved stable remote entanglement between separate quantum devices. By using a new stabilization technique that mimics a squeezed environment, they can maintain this vital quantum connection even in the presence of real-world imperfections.

title: Distributing Stationary Qubit Entanglement through a Nonlocal Squeezed Reservoir
summary: A fully autonomous process is demonstrated that entangles two spatially separated superconducting qubits by coupling them to a shared, quantum-correlated microwave reservoir, offering a robust new platform for high-throughput entanglement distribution in future quantum networks.
